notes: First evidence-collection pass for DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001, covering five searches (SRCH-0001 to SRCH-0005). Established the 2019-2020 drought/trucked-water episode and its resolution, the 2024-2025 Willawarrin treatment plant funding and construction start, and the adjacent $52.9m regional water security package. Three Kempsey Shire Council pages (SRC-0010, SRC-0011, SRC-0012) remain blocked (HTTP 403) to both an automated browser fetch tool and curl with a full browser header set, and are the most likely source of a current 2026 status update - manual browser retrieval is needed to resolve Q-0001. Unpursued leads for a future run: Kempsey Shire Council Public Forum agenda, 20 July 2026 (kempsey.nsw.gov.au, same access block); Macleay Argus 'Kempsey Shire moves to Level 2 water restrictions' (story 6198046, not yet fetched); Mirage News 'Kempsey Tap Water Passes Safety, Below PFAS Limits' (not yet fetched - a different contaminant to this case's iron/manganese focus, relevance not yet assessed).

Follow-up run pursuing RUN-0001's unpursued leads, logged live in data/investigation_notes.json as the work happened (NOTE-0001 to NOTE-0005). Tried the Wayback Machine as an alternate route to SRC-0010 (Kempsey Council current-works page): a snapshot exists and a HEAD request succeeds, but every GET attempt returns HTTP 498 (SRCH-0006); stopped there rather than trying further header/technique variations, since forcing through a bot-detection block is not something this investigation should do regardless of legitimacy of purpose - still an open access gap, not a confirmed absence of information. The Level 2 water restrictions article (EV-0009) pushed the known drought onset back to June 2019. The PFAS article (EV-0010) is the first Bellbrook-specific evidence found since 2020, though it doesn't touch Bellbrook's treatment infrastructure - Q-0002 remains open. The 20 July 2026 Public Forum agenda (kempsey.nsw.gov.au) was not pursued this run - same access block expected; still a lead for a future run with manual browser access.

Continued the operator's request to keep collecting, covering six searches (SRCH-0007 to SRCH-0012), logged live (NOTE-0007 to NOTE-0012). Fully resolved Q-0004 - EV-0011 and EV-0012 confirm the Aug 2024-to-Mar 2025 mayoral change was the routine 2024 NSW Local Government election (Leo Hauville to Kinne Ring, 53.67%) - and closed THR-15. That same finding opened Q-0006: EV-0011's own text gives the election date as '9 September 2024,' which is a Monday and inconsistent with the confirmed statewide Saturday 14 September 2024 polling day; elections.nsw.gov.au (SRC-0018), campbelltown.nsw.gov.au, and sah.org.au (Incapsula-blocked) could not confirm the Kempsey-specific date, so this is logged as an open question rather than a two-sided contradiction, since only one side has citable evidence. EV-0013 (May 2022) pushes the Willawarrin plant's documented history back over two years, and surfaces a separate 'emergency water treatment plant' at Steuart McIntyre Dam (relevant to THR-13). Checked the WaterNSW 2025 compliance report in full - zero mentions of Willawarrin/Bellbrook/Kempsey/Macleay, ruled out as not applicable. Two more Kempsey Council pages (SRC-0021 via Pump Industry Magazine's title, SRC-0022) are flagged for Q-0003 once manual browser access is available. The operator is separately attempting the four blocked kempsey.nsw.gov.au URLs with their own browser tools.

RUN-0004: reconciliation follow-up to RUN-0003 (CHG-0007), carrying forward the non-redundant findings from a separate, unmerged RUN-0003 attempt that duplicated this repository's already-committed mayoral-transition evidence (EV-0011/EV-0012) with a weaker, search-snippet-only version - that duplicate evidence was dropped rather than merged (see NOTE-0013, DEC-0007). Registered SRC-0023 (20 July 2026 Council Public Forum page, confirmed to exist but blocked) and SRC-0024 (Steuart McIntyre Dam Design & Construction tender listing, contractor not named). No new evidence, chronology, or open-question changes - Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, targeting Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 (SRCH-0017 through SRCH-0022). This session's fetch tool returned HTTP 403 on every URL attempted, including a domain and exact URL this repository previously fetched successfully (SRC-0015) and unrelated control URLs (Wikipedia, example.com) - a session-level tooling issue, not a site-specific block, recorded as DEC-0008 so it isn't mistaken for an absence of available sources. As a result no Evidence Register entries were added this run, since none could be preserved/hashed to this repository's existing bar. Registered two new sources for a genuine lead on Q-0005: SRC-0025 (Utility Magazine) and SRC-0026 (Mirage News), both consistently naming 'LC Eire, a partnership between LC Water and Eire Constructions' as the Steuart McIntyre Dam plant's contractor - a strong candidate answer, not yet confirmed against either primary text. Q-0001, Q-0002, Q-0003, and Q-0005 remain open.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request (SRCH-0023 through SRCH-0026). Re-confirmed DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies (retried the exact SRC-0026 URL, still HTTP 403). Found a genuinely new, specific lead for Q-0002/THR-14 (open since RUN-0001): two independent search queries consistently state NSW's 'Aboriginal Communities Water and Sewerage Program' (a $200m joint NSW Government/NSW Aboriginal Land Council initiative since December 2008) lists Bellbrook among its Completed Projects for drinking-water/sewerage upgrade work - registered as SRC-0027, blocked to fetch, not yet an Evidence Register entry. No new information found on Q-0001 or Q-0003 this run. No Evidence Register, Chronology, or Contradiction changes.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request (SRCH-0027 through SRCH-0030), targeting Q-0001, Q-0002, and Q-0003. Retried SRC-0027's URL - DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Continued evidence collection at the operator's request. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies (retried once). Instead of only searching for new material, cross-checked the existing Evidence Register against itself and found CTR-0001: EV-0005 and EV-0006, both NSW Government primary sources published three days apart in March 2025, give different Willawarrin population figures (130 vs 180) - the Contradiction Register's first entry. Also searched for THR-03/THR-04's stated gap (specific ADWG iron/manganese concentration figures) and THR-01's stated gap (pre-2019 history) - neither surfaced anything new. A tangential lead (SRC-0028: a Save Our Macleay River/SCU citizen-science study on arsenic/antimony from historic Hillgrove mining tailings) was registered for completeness but deliberately not linked to a case thread, since it concerns a different contaminant from an upstream source and its relevance to Willawarrin/Bellbrook specifically is unconfirmed.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request (SRCH-0033 through SRCH-0035), targeting Q-0001 and Q-0003 via three angles not tried in prior runs: federal Member for Cowper Pat Conaghan's statements, the 'Your Say Macleay' community engagement platform's Willawarrin page, and a direct delay/pushed-back search given how far past the 'early 2026' target the current date now is. RUN-0010, continuing evidence collection at the operator's request. Retried the fetch tool (miragenews.com and a Wikipedia control URL) - still HTTP 403, DEC-0008 unchanged. Tried three angles new to this investigation: SRC-0028's Hillgrove mining contamination relevance to Willawarrin/Bellbrook specifically (no link found, confirming prior scope caution), a direct NSW Electoral Commission search for Q-0006's disputed election date (found strong corroboration for 14 September 2024, registered as SRC-0029), and an ABS Census search for CTR-0001's disputed population figure (found the 2021 Census figure of 183, close to 180 and registered as SRC-0030). Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, reviewing the parallel RUN-0010 that landed since this session's last push before starting new work. Took a different approach: rather than more search on already-covered ground, computed directly (no external source needed) that 9 September 2024 was a Monday and 14 September 2024 was a Saturday, then found via search that NSW ordinary council elections are legally required to fall on 'the second Saturday in September' - and confirmed by counting Saturdays in September 2024 (7th/14th/21st/28th) that the 14th specifically matches that rule. Registered SRC-0031 (the statute, fetch-blocked) and strengthened Q-0006 with this reasoning. Not closing Q-0006 - a real preserved primary citation is still required and remains blocked (DEC-0008) - but this is the strongest non-primary-source case buildable right now.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, targeting THR-13's contractor/construction-progress gap for the Steuart McIntyre Dam plant. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Found a genuinely new, previously-unregistered event: two independent articles (an NSW Government release and a Port Macquarie News/Macleay Argus syndicated report) confirm a sod-turning/ground-breaking event for this project, placed 'as of July 2025' - consistent with EV-0005's announced mid-2025 start and the equivalent milestone to EV-0006 for the Willawarrin plant. Neither names the contractor, so Q-0005 remains open, but this confirms construction is genuinely underway. Registered as SRC-0032/SRC-0033, both fetch-blocked; updated THR-13's outstanding_work.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request (SRCH-0045/SRCH-0046), targeting THR-03/THR-04's concentration-data gap and a 'Your Say Macleay' quick-poll lead. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. The quick-poll page returned no usable detail. The Drinking Water Database angle initially looked promising (one search claimed 100% compliance for Willawarrin/Bellbrook specifically), but two follow-up searches attributed the actual numeric figures to 'Kempsey and Lower Macleay' and 'South West Rocks' supplies instead, with no Willawarrin-specific table found - an inconsistent, self-contradicting result not solid enough to register per DEC-0007's standard. No new sources, evidence, chronology, or open-question changes.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, trying a genuinely unexplored avenue: Bellbrook's own general history and background, since this register had almost no Bellbrook-specific context beyond its water supply status. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Two independent searches consistently confirmed: Bellbrook gazetted 1892, National Trust heritage village since 1978, 2021 Census population 339 (up from 273 in 2016). Registered as SRC-0034 (Wikipedia) and SRC-0035 (ABS QuickStats), both fetch-blocked, and added to THR-14 as general background context rather than direct evidence of water infrastructure status.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, applying RUN-0014's approach to Willawarrin: searched for the town's own general history for THR-01's stated pre-2019 gap. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Found Kempsey Shire Council's own heritage library page, 'Early history of Willawarrin', cross-confirmed across two independent queries: part of the Toorooka pastoral lease from 1842, first hotel 1893, an important livestock-selling centre 1949-1970. General settlement history, not water-specific, but the earliest documented history found for Willawarrin by over a century. Registered as SRC-0036 (fetch-blocked) and added to THR-01.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, targeting THR-02's gap (Bellbrook's exact trucked-water start date). DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Found a substantial, well-corroborated event not previously registered: the Carrai East Bushfire accelerated 8 November 2019, forcing an evacuation via Bellbrook Public School on 11 November 2019 (approx. 120 people sheltered, homes destroyed), per two independent searches with specific, named, consistent facts. Very likely the specific bushfire behind EV-0002/EV-0003's cited cause. Registered as SRC-0037 (fetch-blocked) and added to THR-01 as a strong unpromoted lead - a real primary source is needed before this can become an Evidence/Chronology entry.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, seeking further corroboration of RUN-0016's Carrai East Bushfire finding rather than a wholly new angle. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies (tried abc.net.au as a new domain - different error, same non-result). Found a third independent source: the NSW Department of Education's December 2019 article 'In the eye of the firestorm', reproducing SRC-0037's core facts with an added specific detail (school lost power/phones at 11:30pm). Registered as SRC-0038 (fetch-blocked); SRC-0037's notes updated to reference this strengthening corroboration. No Evidence Register or Chronology changes.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, following up on the Carrai East Bushfire thread. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Found Willawarrin's own evacuation details (Willawarrin Hall as a Disaster Assistance Welfare Point, homes lost, named residents Terry and Jutta Flynn) and a significant, sensitive finding requiring careful handling: an active NSW Coronial Inquiry proceeding concerning the death of Willawarrin resident Barry Parsons during the same fire. Registered as SRC-0039 (fetch-blocked), recorded with explicit, strictly factual language that no fault or responsibility is stated or implied by any person or body, consistent with the investigation's 'no allegation framing' standard. Deliberately held to a higher promotion bar than usual given the sensitivity - primary-source confirmation is required, not search-snippet corroboration alone.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, trying to strengthen Q-0002's SRC-0027 lead with a more targeted search. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, exploring the Thunggutti Aboriginal Community/Mirriwinni Gardens angle. DEC-0008's fetch-tool outage still applies. Found a substantially valuable, previously-unknown fact: Bellbrook's raw (ground)water supply was contaminated by arsenic/heavy metals from historic Hillgrove-area mining, and a dedicated Bellbrook water treatment plant with arsenic-removal capacity was built around 2009-2010 (~$700,000), per two independent searches. This is a direct, substantive answer to Q-0002 (Bellbrook's own water infrastructure) - genuinely new, distinct infrastructure not previously known to this register. Registered as SRC-0040/SRC-0041 (fetch-blocked); THR-14 and Q-0002 updated substantially.

Continued evidence collection at the operator's request, pursuing a genuinely fresh angle for this repository: whether Kempsey Shire Council is specifically named in NSW Audit Office reporting on at-risk/loss-making councils.
